champion: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
ordered_diagnoses: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction

facts.raw_span: A man in his 70s
history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and moderate pulmonary hypertension
presented with shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and bilateral leg swelling
recurrent palpitations that occurred randomly and were often associated with shortness of breath
medications included aspirin, atorvastatin, amlodipine, tiotropium, and a budesonide-formoterol inhaler
No specific physical examination findings were detailed in the case report
Left ventricular ejection fraction of 40% compared with 60% 2 months prior
25% narrowing of the left anterior descending artery and a distally occluded right coronary artery
Regular narrow complex supraventricular tachycardia with rate of 120 beats per minute
subtle retrograde P waves during tachyarrhythmia
RR interval 800ms, PR interval 200ms
second PAC with prolonged PR interval of 390ms

concepts.why: The patient's ECG shows regular narrow complex supraventricular tachycardia with a rate of 120 beats per minute, and subtle retrograde P waves during tachyarrhythmia, which are characteristic of SVT.

The patient has a history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and cardiac catheterization shows 25% narrowing of the left anterior descending artery and a distally occluded right coronary artery, which are indicative of CAD.

concepts.preferred_label: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction
concepts.why: The patient's left ventricular ejection fraction is 40%, which is reduced, and he presents with shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and bilateral leg swelling, which are symptoms of heart failure.

The patient experiences recurrent palpitations, which can be a symptom of atrial fibrillation, and the ECG shows a supraventricular tachycardia with a rate of 120 beats per minute, which can be a manifestation of AFib.
The patient's reduced left ventricular ejection fraction and history of hypertension and hyperlipidemia suggest cardiomyopathy.

rationales.F02: History of hypertension and hyperlipidemia increases the risk of coronary artery disease.
rationales.F07: Reduced left ventricular ejection fraction is a key feature of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
rationales.F08: Narrowing of the left anterior descending artery and occlusion of the right coronary artery are indicative of coronary artery disease.
rationales.F09: Regular narrow complex supraventricular tachycardia is diagnostic of supraventricular tachycardia.
rationales.F10: Subtle retrograde P waves during tachyarrhythmia support the diagnosis of supraventricular tachycardia.
rationales.F12: Prolonged PR interval is consistent with supraventricular tachycardia.
